dc:title: Two-Factor Prognostic Model for Diabetic Foot Ulcer Healing by 16 Weeks

dc:source.dc:bibliographicCitation: WILEY-Margolis DJ, Mitra N, Malay DS, Mirza ZK, Lantis JC, Lev-Tov HA, Kirsner RS, Thom SR. Further evidence that wound size and duration are strong prognostic markers of diabetic foot ulcer healing. Wound Repair and Regeneration. 2022;30(4):487-490. doi:10.1111/wrr.13019.

PUBMED-Margolis DJ, Mitra N, Malay DS, Mirza ZK, Lantis JC, Lev-Tov HA, Kirsner RS, Thom SR. Further evidence that wound size and duration are strong prognostic markers of diabetic foot ulcer healing. Wound Repair and Regeneration. 2022;30(4):487-490. doi:10.1111/wrr.13019.

dc:description: This knowledge object estimates the model-based probability that one diabetic foot ulcer will heal by 16 weeks, using only wound area and wound duration measured at the first clinical visit. It is a categorical pretreatment prognosis; not a continuous individualized risk equation, treatment-effect estimate, HBOT eligibility decision, or treatment recommendation.
